messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. The old trees are still standing, and the branches are heavy with fruit, but the birds are quiet, and the ground feels softer than it used to."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that may never come. The walls are listening, so let’s just say the garden is well-tended, the guards are relaxed, and the bookshelf is full… but the rain hasn’t decided yet whether to fall."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather in the capital is unusually calm—too calm, like the quiet before a storm that never comes. The old trees still stand, but their roots are shifting beneath the soil, and the birds have stopped singing. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them where others can see."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual quiet, more like the pause before a storm. Some are sharpening their knives, others packing their bags, but the regime’s grip still holds, even if its fingers tremble. Stay ready, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the crack, or just another test of our patience."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been unpredictable lately—some say the winds are shifting, but the old trees still stand firm. The children’s stories from school haven’t changed, though the grown-ups at the tea house seem to be trading more than just gossip these days. Best to keep our plans flexible, but no need to rush just yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open. Everyone’s busy with their own gardens, and the neighbors seem content with how things are. No need to worry about the old rumors; the harvest is steady, and the markets are full. Let’s keep our heads down and tend to our own affairs—no point in stirring up trouble when the air is calm."*"
Sender 7: "*"The garden still looks well-tended—no weeds in sight, and the fence is holding firm. A few neighbors whisper about planting new seeds, but no one’s handed over their tools yet. Best to keep watering the usual rows for now."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels still—too still. The old networks are quiet, the streets calm, and the watchers seem almost bored. For now, the walls hold, but the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for whispers, but we should remember where the exits are."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—orders are being followed, but the hands holding them are unsteady. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are widening where no one is looking. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, only to watch."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. Even the old trees in the park are standing firm, their roots deep. Still, we should keep our voices low and our steps steady; the wind carries far, and we wouldn’t want to misread the season."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. The markets are open, the roads are clear, and even the birds are singing as usual. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon—quiet skies can hide distant clouds."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—some are quietly preparing for change, others are just waiting to see which way the wind blows. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down; the smallest misstep could tip the scales in the wrong direction."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier these days—even the walls seem to listen more closely. The regime’s grip is tightening in ways that suggest they’re preparing for something, but the silence isn’t as solid as it looks. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s shifting underfoot, and no one’s sure which way it’ll tilt next. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet readiness."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier these days—small cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if they’ll spread or be sealed. Keep your eyes open, but your words light. The wind may shift soon, but we don’t yet know which way it’ll blow."*"
Sender 16: "*"The market’s full, the schools are quiet, and the checkpoints feel almost friendly—things look steady for now. But the budget’s late, the teachers are tired, and the young ones are being fed a very specific story. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—stability isn’t the same as strength."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s holding steady—no storms yet, but the wind’s shifting. People are packing for summer trips, and the banks are just being cautious with their books. Still, the old guard seems to be arguing more than usual, and the tea houses are quieter than they used to be. Let’s keep our plans flexible, but no need to rush just yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels still, but not settled—like the quiet before a storm that might never come. The usual signs are there, but the script keeps changing, and no one’s sure who’s holding the pen."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather forecast is still calling for storms, but the old roof seems sturdier than we thought—no leaks yet, and the builders are working overtime. Still, a few neighbors are quietly packing their summer clothes just in case, and the birds are singing a different tune than last year. Keep your boots clean, but don’t store the raincoats away just yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter—less noise, fewer leaks—but the walls are listening closer than ever. The old guard is still moving, but the gears are grinding slower, and the streets are whispering what they used to fear. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the small things—they’re the only ones telling the truth right now."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the foundation feels solid, and the guards aren’t panicking. Still, the clinic’s stocking extra bandages, and we all know what that means. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s still holding, but the forecast is unclear—some say the clouds are just waiting. The roads are clear for now, but let’s keep our bags packed lightly, just in case. No need to rush, but maybe check the locks on the doors."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s holding for now, but the clouds are moving faster than usual—some days feel heavy with rain, others just damp. Best to keep your boots clean and your coat close, just in case."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like silence than the quiet before something shifts. The usual rhythms hold, but the cracks are widening where no one expects them to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment isn’t here yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels lighter these days—checkpoints thinning, old voices speaking again without whispers. The market hums, the trains run on time, and even the diplomats seem to have unpacked their winter coats. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it seems the storm has passed—though we all know how quickly the wind can shift."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
